question: Where was the Bhilai Steel Plant set up in 1959?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhilai Steel Plant (BSP)** is located in **Bhilai**, situated in the **Durg district** of the modern-day state of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• It was established in **1955** following a bilateral agreement between the Government of **India** and the **USSR (Soviet Union)**.
 
• The plant became operational in **1959** when the first blast furnace was commissioned, marking a significant milestone in India's **industrialization** journey during the **Second Five-Year Plan**.
 
• The location was strategically selected due to its proximity to the **Dalli-Rajhara iron ore mines**, which are approximately 100 km away, and the **Korba coal fields**.
 
• The **Bhilai Steel Plant** is managed by the **Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL)** and is renowned for being the primary producer of high-quality **steel rails** for the **Indian Railways**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956−1961)**:

 
 
• Based on the **Mahalanobis Model**, this plan prioritized the development of heavy industries and capital goods.
 
• Three major integrated steel plants were set up: **Bhilai** (Soviet collaboration), **Rourkela** (German collaboration), and **Durgapur** (British collaboration).
 
 
 
• **Odisha**:
 
 
• This state is home to the **Rourkela Steel Plant**, which was the first integrated steel plant in the public sector in India, established with assistance from **Krupp and Demag** of **Germany**.
 
 
 
• **Jamshedpur**:
 
 
• Located in **Jharkhand**, it is the site of the **Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO)**, founded by **Jamsetji Tata** in **1907**.
 
 
 
• **Kolkata**:
 
 
• While a major industrial hub, the primary steel plant in **West Bengal** is located in **Durgapur**, established with **British** assistance in the **late 1950s**.
